before.title: 2.2L Ecotec Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
before.description: Early 2.2L Ecotec (L61) engines have a timing chain oiling deficiency: the oiler nozzle doesn't supply enough oil at low RPM, leading to chain stretch, worn plastic guides, and a weak original tensioner that loses tension. Because the Ecotec is an interference engine, a chain that jumps time or breaks causes pistons to strike valves, often resulting in catastrophic engine damage. GM revised the tensioner/oiler for 2005, after which the problem largely disappeared.
before.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, and guides with the updated parts at the first sign of rattle, before the chain jumps time. Addressing a startup or cold rattle early prevents a destroyed engine. Maintaining clean oil and regular changes reduces wear.
symptoms: Rattling or chain-slap noise, especially on cold startup
Rough running or misfire if chain has jumped time
Check engine light with camshaft/crankshaft correlation codes
Engine won't start or runs very poorly after chain skips

before.title: Ignition Switch Can Unexpectedly Shut Off Engine (GM Defect Recall)
before.description: The ignition switch detent torque is too low, so weight on the key ring, road vibration, or a knee bump can move the switch out of the 'run' position while driving. This shuts off the engine and disables power steering, power brakes, and critically the airbags, which will not deploy in a crash if the switch is out of 'run.' This is the infamous GM ignition switch defect linked to numerous crashes and deaths, and GM established a victim compensation fund.
before.solution: Free dealer replacement of the ignition switch under NHTSA recall 14V047000. As an interim measure GM advised owners to remove all extra weight and the fob from the key ring, using only the bare ignition key. Many cars have already had the recall performed; owners can verify completion via VIN at the GM/NHTSA recall lookup.
symptoms: Engine suddenly stalls or shuts off while driving
Dash warning lights illuminate as power is lost
Loss of power steering and power brake assist after stall
Key turns off if bumped or with heavy keychain
Airbags fail to deploy in a crash

before.title: Inaccurate or Erratic Fuel Gauge (Fuel Level Sensor)
before.description: The fuel level sender inside the tank develops contaminated or worn contacts, sending erratic resistance signals to the gauge. Owners see the needle misread, drop or stick especially below a quarter tank, give false low-fuel warnings, or read empty when fuel remains. Disconnecting the battery can also throw off gauge calibration. The sender is part of the in-tank fuel pump module.
before.solution: Replace the fuel level sensor/sending unit, which generally requires dropping the fuel tank and is most economically done as part of a fuel pump module replacement. Cleaning or adjusting the sender float is a temporary fix at best. A P0463 code points to the level sensor circuit.
symptoms: Fuel gauge reads inaccurately or fluctuates
Needle sticks, drops, or reads empty with fuel in tank
False or premature low-fuel warning light
Gauge misbehaves after a battery disconnect

proposal.title: Inaccurate or Erratic Fuel Gauge (Fuel Level Sensor)
proposal.description: The Ion factory manual shows that fuel level is derived from a float, arm and variable-resistance ceramic card, communicated through the control modules to the cluster. It also provides test values for driving the gauge display. Those documents do not establish a recurring 2003-2007 sender-contact defect, do not say battery disconnection changes calibration and do not prove that the sender is always part of a pump-module replacement. Gauge, sensor, wiring, module communication and float movement require separate testing.
proposal.solution: Compare the displayed level with scan-tool fuel-level data, test the gauge/cluster response using the factory method and inspect the sensor signal, wiring, grounds and module communication. Confirm tank level and float movement before removing the tank. Replace only the failed sender, wiring, cluster or module component identified by testing and follow fuel-system safety procedures. Do not buy a fuel-level sensor, pump module, cluster or wiring from this page; tank design, engine/emissions configuration and electrical diagnosis determine the service part.
symptoms: Fuel gauge reading disagrees with verified tank level
Gauge defaults to Empty during a sensor-circuit or communication fault
Low-fuel message at an implausible tank level
P0463 only when confirmed by the exact diagnostic procedure
affectedSystems: Fuel-level float, arm and ceramic resistor card

before.title: Interior Door Panel and Trim Rattles
before.description: The Ion's interior is prone to rattles and squeaks, most commonly from the door panels. A black plastic reinforcement strip glued along the top of the door panel can separate, and loose window glass/regulator components produce a glass-on-metal rattle over bumps, particularly with the window up or down. The glovebox door and headliner trim are also reported rattle sources. It's a cosmetic/comfort annoyance rather than a safety issue.
before.solution: Remove the affected door panel and re-secure or re-glue the loose plastic reinforcement, add foam/felt to contact points, and check the window regulator and glass run channels. Tightening or padding the glovebox and trim clips resolves the other rattles. Largely a DIY fix.
symptoms: Rattling or buzzing from door panels over bumps
Glass-on-metal rattle with the window up or down
Glovebox door and headliner trim rattle
Loose or separated trim along the top of the door panel

before.title: Key Stuck in Ignition / Worn Lock Cylinder
before.description: Separate from the safety recall, Ion owners frequently report the key sticking in the ignition or refusing to turn fully off, often getting trapped in the ACC position. This stems from a worn ignition lock cylinder, worn key teeth, or a faulty Brake-Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) solenoid that should release the lock when the car is in Park. It can leave the key trapped and accessory power on, risking a dead battery.
before.solution: Replace the ignition lock cylinder and/or worn key; if the interlock is the cause, replace the BTSI solenoid/switch. As a temporary workaround, ensure the shifter is fully in Park and gently jiggle the key. A locksmith or dealer can re-key a new cylinder to the existing key.
symptoms: Key will not come out of the ignition
Key gets stuck in the ACC (accessory) position
Engine won't shut off / accessory power stays on
Key hard to insert, turn, or remove

before.title: Sudden Loss of Electric Power Steering Assist
before.description: The electric power steering (EPS) motor can suddenly lose assist at any time while driving, often mid-turn or at low speed, due to brush debris and oily contamination disrupting the EPS motor. Steering remains mechanically connected but requires much greater effort, especially during parking and low-speed maneuvers, raising crash risk. NHTSA received over 800 Ion complaints and ran a multi-year investigation (PE10-018); the Ion was excluded from GM's 2010 recall and not recalled until 2014.
before.solution: Free replacement of the electric power steering motor under NHTSA recall 14V153000 (began July 2014). 2004-2007 Ions are covered by GM bulletin 14115; 2003 Ions received EPS motor replacement coverage for the life of the vehicle under bulletin 14119. Outside the recall, the fix is the same EPS motor/column assembly replacement.
symptoms: Steering wheel suddenly becomes very hard to turn
Power steering warning light or message
Loss of assist occurs intermittently, sometimes mid-turn
Extra effort needed when parking or at low speed

before.title: VTi CVT Transmission Failure
before.description: The Ion's optional VTi continuously variable transmission (GM's first high-volume CVT) is notoriously unreliable. The steel push-belt and related internals wear or fail, causing slipping, harsh or no engagement, and eventually complete loss of drive. GM halted VTi production in January 2004 due to durability problems and a class-action lawsuit covering roughly 90,000 Ion and Vue vehicles was settled.
before.solution: Failed VTi units typically require full transmission replacement or rebuild; some intermittent no-drive cases were addressed by replacing the case cover assembly, torque converter, and oil cooler lines. The class-action settlement extended coverage to 5 years/75,000 miles from new. Many owners ultimately swap to the conventional automatic or buy a known-good unit.
symptoms: Transmission slipping or flaring under acceleration
Delayed or no engagement into drive or reverse
Whining or unusual transmission noise
Loss of forward motion / car won't move
Check engine or transmission warning
